topics.label: Lecture framing and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets out the lecture's context, aims, and framework before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways mutated to drive proliferation and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how altered extracellular signaling and mutations in downstream pathways promote cancer-cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in hematological and intestinal cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation affects cancer cells, using blood-cell lineages and intestinal epithelium as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and BCL2-family regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how changes in p53, Bax, and BCL2 can prevent cancer cells from undergoing apoptosis.

topics.label: Telomere limits, senescence, and p53 stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening and other stresses trigger growth-arrest safeguards, how tumors can restore telomeres to escape one limit, and how these growth-control mechanisms fit together.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and altered metabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer metabolism is reshaped, including increased glycolysis and metabolite-driven changes to gene regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors induce blood-vessel growth to obtain the oxygen and nutrients needed to expand.

topics.label: Metastatic spread, its inefficiency, and its detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics characterize metastasis as a multistage, inefficient process shaped by circulation and compatibility with secondary sites, and describe ways to detect and monitor it.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion on cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic draws the lecture to a close by recapping its main message and inviting questions.
